records.finding: slugify now takes an arbitrary `separator` but only the HTTP handler restricts it to '-' or '_'. The trim regex hard-codes [-_], so any other separator is left at the ends, and the separator is used as a String.replace replacement string, so `$`-patterns get expanded. Measured: slugify(' a b ', '.') returns '.a.b.' and slugify('a b', '$&') returns 'a b'. The HTTP path cannot hit this because app.js validates against SEPARATORS. It only affects direct callers of the exported function.
records.evidence: Repair e92d8a4, src/slug.js:1-6: SEPARATORS = ['-', '_'] now lives in slug.js and slugify throws RangeError(`separator must be one of: -, _`) before any replace runs; app.js imports the same list, so handler and function share one source of truth. Measured at e92d8a4: slugify(' a b ', '.') and slugify('a b', '$&') both throw RangeError (regression test 'refuses a separator other than - or _', test/slug.test.js:33-36); slugify(' a b ','-') -> 'a-b', ('_') -> 'a_b', default -> 'a-b'. Since only - and _ can reach the replace, the hard-coded [-_] trim and $-expansion are no longer reachable. npm test: 20 pass, 0 fail.

records.finding: The test says it trims a separator 'of either kind', but every non-alphanumeric run, '--' included, is rewritten to '_' before the trim runs. So only the '_' trim is exercised, and a '-' never reaches the trim step. No test covers an explicit `separator=-` or an empty `separator=` (which correctly returns 400) at the HTTP layer.
records.evidence: Repair e92d8a4: the test is renamed 'trims a leading or trailing underscore separator' (test/slug.test.js:25), which is what it exercises; a new test 'trims a leading or trailing hyphen separator' (test/slug.test.js:29-31) asserts slugify('__Hello--World__', '-') === 'hello-world', so a '-' now reaches the trim step. test/app.test.js adds 'GET /slug with separator=- is the default slug' (200, slug 'night-gate') and 'GET /slug with an empty separator is a 400'. All pass under npm test (20/20).
